slides.heading: Run Length Encoding
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Run Length Encoding, an easy strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Encode runs as count+char, with runs longer than 9 split ("AAAAAAAAAAAA" -> "9A3A").
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Encode runs as count plus char, with runs longer than 9 split ("AAAAAAAAAAAA" to "9A3A").

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Count runs of equal characters, but cap each run at nine so the count is always a single digit.
slides.narration: Count runs of equal characters, but cap each run at nine so the count is always a single digit.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Naive: string concatenation in a loop → O(n²)
Cap runs at 9 so counts stay one digit
slides.narration: Concatenating strings in a loop is quadratic in Java. A single pass with a string builder is linear. The twist is capping runs at nine, so the encoded counts are always a single digit and decoding stays unambiguous.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Flush when the character changes or the count hits nine
slides.narration: Step by step. First, scan with a running count. Second, flush when the character changes or the count hits nine. Third, write count then character.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Flush run → 9A
slides.narration: The run of A ends because it hit nine, so we write 9 A.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Flush run → 3A
slides.narration: The run of A ends, so we write 3 A.

slides.narration: The run of B ends, so we write 2 B.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We scan from index one, counting the current run. When the character changes or the run reaches nine, we append the count and the previous character, then reset. After the loop we flush the final run.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Flush the final run after the loop
slides.narration: Twelve A's must become nine A three A, not twelve A. And don't forget to flush the last run after the loop.

bullets: Count runs of equal characters, but cap each run at nine so the count is always a single digit.
